summary: Careful, well‑documented, preregistered confirmatory study that builds and archives a synthetic NetOps task set and deterministic validator and executes a paired comparison of a generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline versus a single‑pass LLM (gpt-5-mini). The run and analysis appear internally consistent and fully archived. The preregistered primary hypothesis was not supported because the baseline was at ceiling (299/300) and the guarded repair stage executed only once, leaving limited opportunity for measurable improvement. The manuscript is transparent and reproducible, but requires a small set of clarifications that can be resolved from the supplied artifacts before I would accept it for finalisation.
required_revisions: Explicitly report the identifier (task/pair id) of the single discordant episode (the one baseline failure) and the SHA‑256 artifact identifier for the single repair provider trace in the manuscript body (these values are present in the archived execution bundle and should be quoted for transparency).

Add an unambiguous statement in the Abstract and Methods that the study used a shared‑initial generation (baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate), that the guarded condition only invoked repair when the deterministic validator failed, and therefore the experiment primarily assesses repair efficacy on identical candidates (not multi‑generation or alternative generation strategies). Cite provider_call_audit stage_counts (shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1) when making this point.

Include the paired contingency counts (n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0) visibly in the main text (Table 1 or inline) and add one sentence explaining how the reported exact McNemar two‑sided p=1.0 arises from these discordant counts and its practical interpretation given the extreme imbalance/ceiling.

Clarify reproducibility detail about deterministic sampling: explicitly state what "temperature=null" and "hosted adapter deterministic sampling mode" mean in practice for reproducing outputs (i.e., whether the provider seeded determinism, which provider settings are required to obtain identical outputs) and point to the exact execution/model_configuration.json and execution/provider_calls entry that a replicator must use to attempt bit‑for‑bit reproduction.
optional_revisions: Briefly reference the preregistered power/sensitivity plan and add one sentence quantifying that the observed baseline success rate (0.9967) invalidates the preregistered detectable effect target (0.10) for N=300 (a numeric sensitivity statement or pointer to the preregistration sensitivity table/artifact is sufficient).

Report an effect‑size summary (Cohen‑h or equivalent for paired proportions) as an exploratory secondary statistic or state why it is not meaningful given the extreme ceiling and lack of discordant pairs.

Replace any OpenAlex placeholder citations in the bibliography with full bibliographic BibTeX entries (the archived BibTeX file exists; ensure the manuscript references a standard formatted bibliography).

Shortly expand the Discussion to more explicitly recommend concrete benchmark adjustments (e.g., higher task difficulty distributions, multi‑generation baseline, larger repair budgets) and link each recommendation to the archived per‑task diagnostics that support it.
